speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: RETURNING to our discussion, since you were camping in Minnesota and have a history of joint pain, did you notice any ticks or insects on your body during the trip? Additionally, have you noticed if the skin lesions appear on your upper body or extremities as well? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and ESR.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme Major secondary to a recent viral or mycoplasma infection, given the painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on acral surfaces and acute arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Blood smear for parasites is not indicated based on these specific skin findings; however, please confirm if any lesions have a central targetoid appearance.
